Rashi on Gittin 24b:10:1.hebrew: הא גדולה מצי מגרש - וכי מפקא ליה, לא חיישינן לאיסור אשת איש למימר: שמא לא לזו ניתן אלא לחברתה, ונפל מידה ומצאתו זו, דהואיל ונקיטא ליה לגיטא בידה, בדידה מחזקינן לה:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:10:1.english: But [the] older [wife] he is able to divorce - And when she produces it, we are not concerned about the prohibition of a married woman [so as] to say: perhaps it was not given to this one, but rather to her counterpart [who shares her name], and it fell from her hand and this one found it; for since she is holding the bill of divorce in her hand, we presume it to be hers:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:11:1.hebrew: מוציאין שטר חוב - אחד מהן שהוציא שטר חוב על אחרים, אין הלוה יכול לומר: "לא ממך לויתי, אלא מפלוני ששמו כשמך, וממנו נפל, ולאו בעל דברים דידי את"; אלא כיון דהאי תפיס לשטרא, גבי ביה:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:11:1.english: [They] can present a promissory note - [If] one of them presents a promissory note against others, the borrower cannot say, "I did not borrow from you, rather from so-and-so whose name is like yours, and it fell from him [and you found it], and you are not my litigant"; rather, since this one is holding the note, he collects with it:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:12:1.hebrew: רישא דקתני כתב לגרש כו' - שאף שמות הבעלים שוין, תידוק נמי: הא ראשון שנכתב לשמו מגרש ביה, וכי מפקא ליה, לא אמרינן משום חומרא דאשת איש, שמא לא בעלה של זו כתבו אלא האחר:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:12:1.english: The earlier clause that teaches, "[If one] wrote [a bill of divorce] to divorce, etc." - where even the husbands' names are identical — you should also infer: [only the second man cannot divorce with it,] whereas the first [man], for whose sake it was written, may divorce with it, and when [his wife] produces it [as proof of divorce], we do not say, due to the stringency of [the laws of] a married woman, "Perhaps it was not this woman's husband who wrote it, but rather the other [man]"?!

Rashi on Gittin 24b:12:2.hebrew: הא אמרינן - במתני' דגט פשוט בב"ב (דף קעב.): "שני יוסף בן שמעון שהיו בעיר אחת אין יכולין להוציא שטר חוב זה על זה, ולא אחר יכול להוציא עליהן שטר חוב", דאמר ליה: לא אני לויתי ממך, אלא חברי לוה ממך ומסר לך שטר זה. דאע"ג דפליגי תנאי התם במוציאין שטר חוב על אחרים ולא חיישינן לנפילה, מודו דאין אחרים מוציאין עליהן כדפרישית. הכא נמי לימא: לא בעלה כתבו, אלא יוסף בן שמעון אחר כתבו לאשתו, ונמלך ולא גירשה, והשליכו לאיבוד מדעת, ולקחתו זו שהיא רוצה להתגרש:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:12:2.english: Didn’t we say - In the Mishnah of [the chapter] Get Pashut in Bava Batra (172a): "Two [men named] Yosef ben Shimon who were in one city cannot produce a promissory note against one another, nor can another [person] produce a promissory note against them," because he can say to him, "It was not I who borrowed from you, rather my fellow borrowed from you and handed this note to you." For even though the Tannaim disagree there regarding [their] producing a promissory note against others — and we are not concerned about [it] having fallen — they [all] agree that others cannot produce [a note] against them, as I have explained. Here too, one could say: "Her husband did not write it, rather another Yosef ben Shimon wrote it for his wife, and reconsidered and did not divorce her, and intentionally threw it away to be lost, and this [woman] who wishes to be divorced took it":

Rashi on Gittin 24b:13:1.hebrew: בעדי מסירה - שמכירים את שניהם ומעידין שראו שזה מסר לזו, אבל בעדי חתימה לא, כדאמרינן: שמא נמלך זה שכתבו וחתמו ולא גרש את אשתו, ומסרו לזו אשת חבירו:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:13:1.english: By witnesses of transmission - who recognize both of them and testify that they saw that this [man] delivered [the bill of divorce] to this [woman]; but by witnesses of signing [alone, it is] not [valid], as we said [earlier]: perhaps this [man] who wrote it and had it signed reconsidered and did not divorce his wife, and [instead] gave it to this [other woman], the wife of his fellow:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:14:1.hebrew: הכא נמי בעדי מסירה - וליכא למיחש שמא לחברתה נמסר, אבל בעדי חתימה לעולם אימא לך דחיישינן שמא את חברתה גירש וחיישינן לנפילה, וגבי שטרי חוב נמי אין יכולין להוציא שטר חוב על אחרים, דחיישינן לנפילה:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:14:1.english: Here too, [it is] with witnesses of transmission - and there is no [need] to be concerned that perhaps it was transmitted to the other [wife]. However, with witnesses of signature, I can still say to you that we are concerned that perhaps he divorced the other [wife], and we are concerned about [the document] having fallen. And regarding promissory notes as well, they cannot produce a promissory note [to collect] against others, because we are concerned about [it] having fallen:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:15:1.hebrew: כולן - כל הגיטין השנויין במשנתנו, אע"פ שפסולין לגרש להתירן לינשא:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:15:1.english: All of them - [This refers to] all the bills of divorce taught in our Mishnah, even though they are invalid for divorcing [so as] to permit them to marry:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:15:2.hebrew: פוסלין - הן אותה מן הכהונה; אם בעלה כהן, נפסלה עליו משום גרושה:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:15:2.english: Disqualify - They [disqualify] her from the priesthood; if her husband is a priest, she becomes disqualified to him on account of [being] a divorcee:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:15:3.hebrew: חוץ מן הראשון - שלא נכתב לשם גירושין כלל, אבל הנך בתראי פסלי, דריח הגט פוסל בכהונה, דתניא בפרק בתרא (לקמן גיטין דף פב:): האומר לאשתו "הרי את מגורשת ממני ואי את מותרת לכל אדם", פסלה מן הכהונה, שנאמר "ואשה גרושה מאישה" — אפילו לא נתגרשה אלא מאישה, ולאחרים לא הותרה, פסולה לכהונה:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:15:3.english: Except for the first - Because it was not written for the sake of divorce at all; however, those latter [bills of divorce] disqualify [her], for the "scent of a get" disqualifies [a woman] from [marrying into] the priesthood, as it was taught in a Baraita in the last chapter (later, Gittin 82b): One who says to his wife, "Behold, you are divorced from me, but you are not permitted to any [other] man," disqualifies her from the priesthood, as it is stated [Leviticus 21:7]: "and a woman divorced from her husband" — even if she was divorced only from her husband, and was not permitted to others, she is disqualified from the priesthood:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:15:4.english: Even [the] first [bill of divorce] - because it has [the] scent of a bill of divorce:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:16:1.hebrew: חליצה פסולה פסולה ופוסלתה - כל מקום ששנינו ביבמות "חליצה פסולה", פסולה להתירה לשוק, אבל פוסלת היא אותה מן האחין שלא תתייבם עוד, דקמו עלה ב"כיון שלא בנה שוב לא יבנה", דלא כתיב "אשר לא בנה את בית אחיו", אלא "אשר לא יבנה" (דברים כ״ה:ט׳), כיון שחלץ, שוב לא יבנה:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:16:1.english: An invalid ḥalitza is invalid and disqualifies her - Wherever we learned in [Tractate] Yevamot [the phrase] "an invalid ḥalitza," [it means] it is invalid to permit her [to marry] into the general public, but it disqualifies her from the brothers so that she may no longer enter into levirate marriage, for they [the Sages] established regarding it [the rule]: "Once he has not built, he may never again build," for it is not written "who did not build [banah] his brother's house," rather "who will not build [yivneh]" (Deuteronomy 25:9) — once he has performed ḥalitza, he may never again build:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:17:1.hebrew: שמאל - חלצה בשמאל, אמרינן ביבמות (דף קד.): פסולה; וכן חלצה בלילה, פסולה:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:17:1.english: Left [foot] - [If] she performed ḥalitza on the left [foot], we say in Yevamot (104a) [that] it is invalid; and similarly, [if] she performed ḥalitza at night, it is invalid:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:17:2.hebrew: ופוסלת - דשם חליצה עלה, אלא שלא נעשית בהכשירה, דיליף "רגל" "רגל" ממצורע דכתיב "ימנית", ולילה נמי נפקא לן התם:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:17:2.english: And it disqualifies [her] - because the status of chalitzah applies to it, except that it was not performed in its proper manner — for [the Gemara] derives [a verbal analogy between] "foot" [and] "foot" from a metzora, regarding whom "right" is written, and [the disqualification of] night is also derived there:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:1:1.english: Older and younger - [This is] not specifically [so]:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:2:1.hebrew: לאיזו שארצה אגרש פסול לגרש בו - דאין ברירה, דלא אמרינן הוברר הדבר דבשעת כתיבה היה דעתו לזו, והרי נכתב לשמה:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:2:1.english: For whichever [one] that I will want I will divorce, [it is] unfit to divorce with it - because there is no retroactive designation, for we do not say that the matter has been clarified [retroactively] that at the time of writing his intention was for this [wife], and [that] it was thus written for her sake:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:3:1.english: But the first clause - where it teaches, "So-and-so divorced So-and-so," etc.:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:3:2.hebrew: במאי - אי לאו הכי, דאותו פלוני כתב לגרש את אשתו ונמלך:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:3:2.english: With what [case] - If not this [case], that that certain person wrote [a bill of divorce] to divorce his wife and reconsidered[, with what case is the first clause dealing?]:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:4:1.english: To learn - to write bills of divorce:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:4:2.hebrew: מקרין - הגדולים מקרים לתלמידיהם: "כך וכך כשיבא גט לפניך כתבהו", והזכירו שם אינש בעלמא; אלמא בתלמידים עסקינן:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:4:2.english: Dictating - The senior [scribes] dictate to their students: "[Write] such-and-such; when a bill of divorce comes before you, write it [this way]," and they mention the name of just any person; thus, we are dealing with students.

Rashi on Gittin 24b:5:1.english: Not [only] this [bill of divorce] that was not written for the sake of any divorce - rather, [it was written] to practice:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:5:2.hebrew: אלא אף זה שנכתב לשם גירושין - גמורין ונמלך, פסול:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:5:2.english: But even this [bill of divorce], which was written for the sake of divorce - [that is, for] an actual [divorce], and [the husband] reconsidered, [it is] invalid:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:6:1.hebrew: ולא זה בלבד שנכתב שלא לשם גירושין - של אדם זה, פסול; אלא אף זה — דהיו לו שתי נשים, שנכתב לשם גירושין דהאי גברא — פסול, הואיל ונכתב שלא לשם גירושין של זו:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:6:1.english: And not only this [bill of divorce], which was not written for the sake of divorce - of this man, is unfit; rather, even that [case] — where he had two wives, [and it] was written for the sake of divorce for this man — is unfit, since it was written not for the sake of the divorce of this [particular wife]:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:9:1.hebrew: וסיפא - מאי קמ"ל? הא אשמעינן כבר דגירושין דידיה ודידה בעינן:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:9:1.english: And the last clause [of the Mishnah] - What does it teach us? [The Mishnah] has already taught us that we require [a] divorce [to be written] for him and for her:

Rashi on Gittin 24b:9:2.hebrew: דאין ברירה - דלא תימא הוברר דבשעת כתיבה נמי דעתיה אהא, ואיכא גירושין דידיה ודידה:
Rashi on Gittin 24b:9:2.english: That there is no [retroactive] clarification - so that you should not say it was [retroactively] clarified that at the time of writing as well his intention was for this [wife], and [thus] there is a divorce for him and for her:

Tosafot on Gittin 24b:13:1.hebrew: בעדי מסירה ור' אלעזר היא - אבל לר' מאיר, בעינן שיהא מוכח מתוך החתימה שנכתב לשם זה האיש ואשה זו, ולא מהני עדי מסירה. וההיא דהמגרש (לקמן גיטין פו:): "שנים ששלחו ב' גיטין ושמותיהן שוין, נותן שניהם לזו ושניהם לזו", וקאמר ר' ירמיה בגמרא: "הא דלא כר' אלעזר", משמע דכר' מאיר ניחא — התם מיירי כדפרשי' לעיל, כשכתבו דורות או סימן או כהן שניכר מתוך החתימה, ועדי מסירה אין מכירין באבותיהן או בסימן הכתוב. וא"ת: למאן דחייש לקמן בפרקין (גיטין דף כז.) לשני שוירי ולשני יוסף בן שמעון אע"ג דלא הוחזקו, א"כ לר"מ, יפסלו כל הגיטין, דלא משכחת תו שום גט שיהא מוכח מתוכו! ואומר ר"י, דדוקא בגט הנמצא הוא דחייש שמא מאחר נפל; אבל חשיב שפיר מוכח מתוכו, כיון דלא הוחזקו אלא שוירי א' ויוסף בן שמעון אחד. ואם תאמר: דתנן בפרק גט פשוט (ב"ב דף קסז:): "כותבין גט לאיש אע"פ שאין אשתו עמו", ופריך בגמרא: "וליחוש לשני יוסף בן שמעון הדרים בעיר אחת, דלמא ממטי לה גיטא לאיתתיה דהאיך", ומשני: "הכי אמר רב, שני יוסף בן שמעון הדרים בעיר אחת אין מגרשין אלא זה בפני זה". והשתא היכי מיירי? אי בלא הוחזקו — הא מסקינן לקמן דלא חיישינן! ואי בהוחזקו — א"כ לר"מ אפי' זה בפני זה אין מגרשין עד שיכתבו כהן או דורות או שום סימן, ואז ליכא למיחש למידי; ואי לר' אלעזר — הא עדי מסירה ידעי שפיר אם זו היא אשתו או לאו, כדאמר הכא! ואומר ר"י, דאין עדי מסירה מדקדקים לראות אם זו אשתו, כיון שמכירים שמו ושמה וכתוב בגט שמו ושמה, ולא חיישי' שמא יתננו לאשת חבירו ששמו כשמו ושמה כשמה, וגם לא מסקי אדעתייהו להבחין אם יש יוסף בן שמעון אחר בעיר; וכשבאה לב"ד להתירה להנשא, מעידים עדי מסירה בפני ב"ד שראו שבעלה נתן לה גט, אע"פ שלא דקדקו אם היא היתה אשתו. ולהכי פריך: "ניחוש דלמא ממטי לה גיטא לאיתתיה דהאי" — דאפילו אין יודעין הכותבין אם הוחזקו, אין להם לכתוב, דזימנין דהוחזקו ולא ידעי. ומשני: "שני יוסף כו', אין מגרשין אלא זה בפני זה" — וכשבאה לבית דין להתירה, שיילי ב"ד לעדי מסירה אם היו שם שני יוסף בן שמעון. ולא רצה לתרץ דאין מגרשין אלא א"כ מכירין עדים שזו היא אשתו, דאין זו תקנה טובה, דאם כן בטורח ימצאו עדי מסירה:
Tosafot on Gittin 24b:13:1.english: With witnesses of transmission, and it is [in accordance with] Rabbi Elazar - But according to Rabbi Meir, we require that it be evident from within the signed document that it was written for the sake of this man and this woman, and witnesses of transmission are not effective. And [as for] that [Mishnah] in [chapter] HaMegaresh (below, Gittin 86b): "Two [men] who sent two bills of divorce and their names are identical — he gives both of them to this [woman] and both of them to that [woman]," and Rabbi Yirmeya says in the Gemara: "This is not in accordance with Rabbi Elazar," implying that according to Rabbi Meir it is fine — there it is speaking as we explained above, when they wrote generations [of ancestry], or a distinguishing mark, or "Kohen," so that it is recognizable from within the signed document, while the witnesses of transmission do not recognize their ancestors or the written distinguishing mark. And if you will say: According to the one who is concerned below in our chapter (Gittin 27a) for two [towns named] Shviri and for two [men named] Yosef ben Shimon even though they were not established [to exist], if so, according to Rabbi Meir, all bills of divorce will be invalidated, for you will no longer find any bill of divorce that is evident from within itself! And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that it is specifically in the case of a found bill of divorce that he is concerned lest it fell from another; however, it is properly considered evident from within itself, since there were established [to be] only one Shviri and one Yosef ben Shimon. And if you will say: For we learned in a Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] Get Pashut (Bava Batra 167b): "One may write a bill of divorce for a man even though his wife is not with him," and [the Gemara] raises a difficulty in the Gemara: "But let us be concerned for two [men named] Yosef ben Shimon who live in one city — perhaps he will bring the bill of divorce to the wife of that other one!" And it answers: "Thus said Rav: Two [men named] Yosef ben Shimon who live in one city may divorce only one in the presence of the other." Now, what case is [that Gemara] speaking of? If [it is] where [two such men] were not established [to exist] — behold, we conclude below that we are not concerned! And if [it is] where they were established [to exist] — if so, according to Rabbi Meir, even one in the presence of the other they may not divorce until they write "Kohen" or generations or some distinguishing mark, and then there is nothing to be concerned about; and if [it is] according to Rabbi Elazar — behold, the witnesses of transmission know well whether this is his wife or not, as [the Gemara] says here! And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that witnesses of transmission are not meticulous to see whether this [woman] is his wife, since they recognize his name and her name and his name and her name are written in the bill of divorce, and they are not concerned lest he give it to his fellow's wife whose name is like his name and whose name is like her name, and also it does not enter their minds to discern whether there is another Yosef ben Shimon in the city; and when she comes to the court to permit her to marry, the witnesses of transmission testify before the court that they saw that her husband gave her a bill of divorce, even though they were not meticulous [to check] whether she was his wife. And therefore [the Gemara] asks: "Let us be concerned lest he bring the bill of divorce to the wife of this [other] one" — for even [when] the scribes do not know whether [two such men] were established [to exist], they should not write [it], for sometimes they were established and [the scribes] do not know. And it answers: "Two Yosefs, etc., they may divorce only one in the presence of the other" — and when she comes to the court to permit her [to remarry], the court asks the witnesses of transmission whether there were two [men named] Yosef ben Shimon there. And [the Gemara] did not want to answer that they may divorce only if the witnesses recognize that this is his wife, because that is not a good enactment, for if so, witnesses of transmission would be found [only] with difficulty:

Tosafot on Gittin 24b:2:1.hebrew: לאיזו שארצה אגרש בו פסול - בגמרא מפרש משום דאין ברירה. ואומר ר"י דאפי' מאן דסבר בעלמא יש ברירה, הכא מודה, משום ד"וכתב לה" לשמה משמע שיהא מבורר בשעת כתיבה. וכן משמע בגמרא, דקאמר: "אי איתמר בהא, בהא קאמר ר' יוחנן דאין ברירה, משום דבעינן לה לשמה". משמע, אע"ג דבעלמא יש ברירה, הכא פסול משום דכתיב "וכתב לה":
Tosafot on Gittin 24b:2:1.english: For whichever [one] I will want, I will divorce [her] with it; [it is] unfit - In the Gemara, [it] explains [that this is] because there is no retroactive designation. And the Ri says that even one who holds in general [that] there is retroactive designation concedes here, because "and he shall write for her" [meaning] for her sake implies that it must be clarified at the time of writing. And so it is implied in the Gemara, which says: "If it was stated regarding this [case], regarding this [case] Rabbi Yoḥanan says that there is no retroactive designation, because we require [it to be written] 'for her' [meaning] for her sake." This implies [that] even though in general there is retroactive designation, here it is unfit because it is written, "and he shall write for her":
